en.title: Dashes in Dialogue
en.summary: Learn how dashes mark spoken dialogue in Romanian text and how to pause when reading them aloud.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: A dash does not make a sound by itself. Instead, it shows that a person starts talking. You pause briefly before you speak. Your voice often rises or sounds lively when speech begins. Listen to (Bună) /bu.ˈnə/, which means hi. The dash before it signals fresh, spoken words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Stop for a tiny moment at the dash. Take a breath and lift your pitch slightly. Speak the first word with fresh energy. In (Bună) /bu.ˈnə/, keep your voice warm and clear. Your tone should sound friendly and natural. Then continue smoothly with the rest of the sentence.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look at the start of a written line. A long dash marks direct speech in text. You do not see quotation marks here. When someone answers, a new line starts with another dash. For example, an answer can be (Da) /da/, which means yes.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not look for quotation marks around spoken turns. Dashes replace them at the start of lines. Do not read without a tiny pause at the dash. A short break helps the listener hear the shift. A short reply like (Nu) /nu/, which means no, needs this clear start.
